13420 THE PRESIDENT
The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title I I  of 
such Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance 
with the provisions of Section 206 of such Act. W ith respect to the 
dispute giving rise to the strike at Evendale, Ohio, plant it shall report 
on or before October 18th, 1966, and with respect to the dispute or 
disputes resulting in any other such strike, it shall report as soon as 
possible.
Upon the submission of its report or reports, the Board shall con­
tinue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required 
under such Act.

Executive Order No. 11314
CREATING A BOARD OF INQUIRY TO REPORT ON CERTAIN LABOR
DISPUTES AFFECTING THE MILITARY JET ENGINE INDUSTRY, MILI­
TARY AIRCRAFT INDUSTRY, MILITARY ARMAMENT INDUSTRY AND
MILITARY ELECTRONICS INDUSTRY OF THE UNITED STATES
W H E R E A S, there have existed certain labor disputes between Gen­
eral Electric Company and certain of its employees represented by : 
International Union of Electrical Radio and Machine Workers, 
A F L -C IO ; International Association of Machinists and Aerospace 
Workers, A F L -C IO ; International Union, United Automobile, Aero­
space and A gricultural Implement Workers of America, A F L -C IO  ; 
International Union, Allied Industrial W orkers of America, A F L - 
CIO ; International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers, A F L -C IO ; 
Sheet Metal W orkers’  International Association, A F L -C IO ; Ameri­
can Federation of Technical Engineers, A F L -C IO  ; American F lint 
Glass W orkers’  Union of North America, A F L -C IO ; United 
Electrical Radio and Machine W orkers of America; United Associa­
tion of Journeymen and Apprentices of the Plumbing and Pipe F itting 
Industry of the United States and Canada, A F L -C IO  ; United Steel­
workers of America, A F L -C IO ; International Union of Operating 
Engineers, A F L -C IO  ; International Brotherhood of Teamsters, 
Chauffeurs, Warehousemen and Helpers of America ; Pattern Makers’  
League of North America, A F L -C IO  ; International Brotherhood of 
Firemen and Oilers, A F L -C IO ; Syracuse Draftsmens Union; and
W H E R E A S, although a tentative resolution of these disputes was 
arrived at by the parties, or some of them, nevertheless there is a strike 
at the Evendale, Ohio, plant of General Electric Company by Local 
No. 647 of the International Union of the United Automobile, Aero­
space and Agricultural Implement Workers of America, A F L -C IO , 
and Locals 34 and 912 of the International Association of Machinists 
and Aerospace Workers, A F L -C IO , and there exists a threat that 
there will be further strikes at General Electric Company plants by 
one or more of the aforesaid international unions or local units 
thereof ; and
W H E R E A S, the existing strike at the Evendale, Ohio, plant of 
General Electric Company will, in my opinion, if permitted to con­
tinue, affect a substantial p art of the m ilitary jet engine industry, 
which industry is engaged in trade, commerce, transportation, trans­
mission, or communication among the several states or with foreign 
nations, or engaged in the production of goods for commerce, and which 
strike, if permitted to continue, will imperil the national safety ; and
W H E R E A S, threatened strikes at other General Electric Company 
plants will, in my opinion, if allowed to occur, affect a substantial 
p art of the military jet engine industry, m ilitary aircraft industry, 
m ilitary armament industry and m ilitary electronics industry, which 
industries are engaged in trade, commerce, transportation, transmis­
sion, or communication among the several states or with foreign na­
tions, or engaged in the production of goods for commerce, and which 
threatened strikes, if permitted to occur, will imperil the national 
safety ;
NOW T H E R E F O R E  by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 206 of the Labor Management Relations Act of 1947 (61 Stat. 
155; 29 U.S.C. 176), I  hereby create a Board of Inquiry, consisting 
of Mr. David L. Cole, Chairman, Mr. John Dunlop and Mr. Jacob 
Seidenberg, whom I  appoint to inquire into the issues involved in 
these disputes.
FEDERAL REGISTER, VOL. 31, NO. 202— TUESDAY, OCTOBER 18, 1966

versions.research_rationale:
EO 11314 (1966-10-17, 31 FR 13419) creates a board of inquiry under section 206 of the Labor Management Relations Act, 1947 to inquire into certain labor disputes between General Electric Company and certain of its employees, including a strike at the Evendale, Ohio, plant, affecting the military jet engine, military aircraft, military armament and military electronics industries, appoints its named members, gives it the powers and duties of Title II of that Act, directs it to report on or before October 18th, 1966 for the Evendale dispute and as soon as possible for any other strike, and provides that after its report the board continues in existence to perform other functions the Act requires. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11314.txt, 31 FR 13419, PDF pages 11-12). The dossier's inventory is incomplete or split mid-sentence (it omits the order's opening paragraphs or divides the report date from its year), so I replaced it with one clause covering the whole printed order from its heading to its last sentence. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25) revokes the order by number. The first end is that express revocation. The board's report date and any later discharge of the board are not established by a held reviewed source and are not ends. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own terms: the order sets a report date ('report on or before October 18th, 1966 for the Evendale dispute and as soon as possible for any other strike') and says the board continues in existence after reporting to perform functions required under the Act; it states no end date. A report date is a deadline, not an end. The board's actual report, any settlement and any discharge of the board under Title II of the Act are not established by a held reviewed source, so no earlier end is claimed. The by-number scan lists no held later order citing this order other than EO 12553, which names it; the catalog note, the U.S. Code and the eCFR searches add nothing earlier.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order creates the board, appoints its named members and sets its report date. The appointments are one-time acts whose surviving consequence (the members' service and the board's report) is a completed fact; no held source shows when the board was discharged, so no earlier end is asserted. The order creates no fund, delegation or continuing authority outside the board and survives only as long as the order does.","savings_check":"Savings: none in EO 12553 or in this order; the board's acts are completed facts and nothing continues independently of the order.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 revokes the order in full; its table entry carries no 'in part' limit, so the single corrected clause ends on the revocation date. No held source records a partial amendment."}

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording (searched in the full held text), so the revocation leaves no part of this order in operation. The board's creation, appointments, report and any later discharge are completed facts whose dates are not held, and the order created no continuing right or fund.

first_end.mechanism: express revocation by EO 12553: its operative sentence ends with the words "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and is followed by a two-column table headed 'No. Subject' whose entry "11314 Creating a board of inquiry to report on labor disputes affecting the military jet engine, military" names this order by number; EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the full held text was searched for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending), so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986). The signing-date reading is an inference from the order's heading and signature block, not express wording.
